question.problem:
What are the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola $y=-6{x}^{2}+36x-50?$

The coordinates of the vertex are
$($
{{field-1}}
,
{{field-2}}
$).$
question.worked_solution:
The parabola's vertex lies on the symmetry axis, so we will start by computing the axis of symmetry. 

The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=a{x}^{2}+bx+c$ is given by

$$
x=-\frac{b}{2a}.
$$

Substituting $a=-6$ and $b=36$ into the formula for the axis of symmetry, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-\frac{36}{2(-6)} \\  & =-\frac{36}{(-12)} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the axis of symmetry is $x=3.$ This also represents the $x$-coordinate of the vertex. To find the $y$-coordinate of the vertex, we substitute $x=3$ into the original equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-6{x}^{2}+36x-50 \\  & =-6(3)^{2}+36(3)-50 \\  & =-54+108-50 \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vertex is at $(3,4).$
